profile.campus: Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster (SFO1-SFO4, formerly Centersquare, formerly Evoque Data Center Solutions)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.address: 1500/1550 Space Park Drive, Santa Clara, CA
profile.reading:
This building is the easternmost of two structures that Csquare markets together as SFO4, part of its four building Silicon Valley campus cluster at 1500 and 1550 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, California, sitting roughly 300 feet from its sibling SFO4 building to the west. Csquare's own SEC registration prospectus lists two distinct rentable units under the SFO4 code, SFO4_A at 21,724 rentable square feet, leased, 86.8 percent occupied as of March 31, 2026, and SFO4_B at 35,754 rentable square feet, company owned and fully occupied. Which suffix maps to this building rather than to its western neighbor could not be confirmed this session, so no individual floor area or occupancy figure is written to this record, and this row should be read as a genuinely separate structure rather than a duplicate map entry for the same building.

Csquare's own facility page gives the combined SFO4 code, both buildings together, as 57,450 square feet of raised floor, 43.1 megawatts of utility power, 12.3 megawatts of UPS protected capacity, and 20.5 megawatts of generator capacity, certified to SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, LEED Gold, and ENERGY STAR standards, with three carrier neutral providers on site. Those figures describe the SFO4 pair as a whole rather than this building alone and are recorded here as campus context only.

Csquare, Inc., which trades on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, reports that it began operations in January 2019 as BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, a name that later gave way to Evoque Data Center Solutions under Brookfield affiliated ownership, then Centersquare, then Csquare, converting to a Delaware corporation on June 15, 2026 shortly before an initial public offering on July 16, 2026 priced at 21 dollars a share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross. Brookfield Corporation kept about 69 percent of voting power after the offering, making Csquare a controlled company under New York Stock Exchange rules. As of March 31, 2026 the company's portfolio spanned 64 sites across 21 metro markets in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity, and its own prospectus flags California, alongside Boston, as a market where power costs run higher and more volatile than the company average.

Across the full four building Silicon Valley cluster that includes this building, Csquare reports more than 273,000 square feet of combined raised floor, 129.4 megawatts of combined utility power and 16 unique carrier networks. No tenant is named for either SFO4 unit in any source reviewed, and the SFO airport code applied to this Santa Clara and Sunnyvale cluster, despite sitting roughly 40 miles south of San Francisco International Airport, reflects a Bay Area colocation naming convention inherited from the site's earlier CenturyLink and Savvis heritage rather than any current geographic logic.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO4 in Santa Clara publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space, but does not separate IT load from total facility draw, leaving usable compute capacity unstated.

The facility holds six certifications spanning financial controls, information security, payment systems, federal compliance, and sustainable building standards. These qualify the campus to host regulated workloads, though which tenants invoke which certifications remains unpublished. The certifications themselves tell nothing about current occupancy, utilization, or whether the facility is built out or still under construction.

California has 103 data center facilities in this registry, yet only seven publish megawatt figures. SFO4's 129.4 MW exceeds the published capacity of every other facility in the state for which a number exists. This ranking is an artifact of extreme scarcity in disclosed capacity data. It does not indicate whether SFO4 is truly the largest facility in California by power, only that most operators do not publish this figure at all. The real constraint on AI scaling in the region remains invisible in public data.
